focus-revealed-instruction-not-honored/c.mechanism: The password field's focus handler was copy-pasted from the email field and never re-targeted: it adds .show to #email-hint, so focusing #pw reveals the EMAIL field's domain hint, not the password rules. The password's own complexity-rules node (#pw-hint) is class='hint' (display:none), carries aria-hidden='true', has no aria-describedby pointing at it, and nothing ever adds .show — so it is pruned from the AX tree and never shown to anyone. Both populations lose the password field's only instruction.
focus-revealed-instruction-not-honored/c.scenario: Fintech (Tellard) wallet signup. The password field's only instruction is its complexity rules ('12+ chars, 1 number, 1 symbol') in #pw-hint. The password's focus handler was copied from the email field and still targets #email-hint, so focusing the password reveals the email-domain hint; #pw-hint is display:none + aria-hidden and never un-hides, so the actual rules reach no one.
focus-revealed-instruction-not-honored/c.note: Page genuinely demonstrates the aspect (password's only instruction never perceivable on focus), but the prose described the wrong concrete mechanism: a classList.remove('hide') vs 'hidden' no-op. The real bug is a copy-pasted handler targeting #email-hint plus an aria-hidden, never-shown #pw-hint.

group-label-needed-but-absent-generalize.mechanism: Two structurally identical attendee blocks have byte-identical inner labels (Full name / Email for the ticket / T-shirt size). The only disambiguator is the title 'Attendee 1' / 'Attendee 2', which is REAL DOM text inside a styled <div class='ticket-bar'> — but it is not a <legend>, not a heading, and is not referenced by the <section> or any control via aria-labelledby. So it is part of no accessible name; an AT user in forms mode hears two identical 'Full name…' groups with no group boundary announced.
group-label-needed-but-absent-generalize.scenario: DevNorth 2026 conference-ticket checkout collects two attendees in two structurally identical cards with byte-identical inner labels (Full name / Email for the ticket / T-shirt size); the only thing naming each block — the 'Attendee 1' / 'Attendee 2' bar — is a decorative <div>, not a legend/heading and not bound to the group via aria, so the required group description is present visually but presented to no one as a label.
group-label-needed-but-absent-generalize.note: Page demonstrates the aspect, but the prose described the wrong concrete instance: it claimed a Cirruswing Air 'Passenger 1/2' badge drawn via CSS .pax-head::before{content:'Passenger ' counter(pax)} with an empty DOM div. The page is actually DevNorth 'Attendee 1/2' as REAL DOM text in a non-semantic div.ticket-bar.

instruction-visually-orphaned-from-its-f.mechanism: The security-answer field's matching rule (case-sensitive, spaces significant) lives in #answer-rule, correctly associated via aria-describedby, but the span is class='sr-only' (1px clipped box; NOT display:none, NOT aria-hidden). It stays in the accessibility tree so screen readers announce it, yet it is invisible on screen — a sighted user sees the 'Your answer' field with no cue that case and spaces matter. Orphaned from sighted users by visually-hidden styling.
instruction-visually-orphaned-from-its-f.scenario: Tidewater Federal Credit Union 'Reset your security answer' page. The security-answer field has a strict case-sensitive, space-significant matching rule (#answer-rule). The rule is wired via aria-describedby but rendered .sr-only, so it is announced to AT yet never shown to sighted users, who type the answer however they remember it and are rejected.
instruction-visually-orphaned-from-its-f.note: Page demonstrates the aspect (instruction not presented to all users), but the prose described a different concrete page/mechanism: a Brightleaf Supply Co. purchase-order field whose format hint sits in a closed-by-default <details> disclosure. The actual orphaning is a .sr-only visually-hidden span on a credit-union security-answer field.

instruction-visually-orphaned-from-its-f.mechanism: The Security-code (CVC) format note (#cvc-note: 3 digits on the back, 4 on the front for Amex) is correctly tied to #cvc via aria-describedby and follows it in source order, but .cvc-note is position:absolute; left:0; bottom:0 within the payment row, so it paints in the empty band beneath the full-width 'Card number' field above — visually reading as the Card number's instruction, while the Security code box (upper-right) appears to have none. Orphaned by wrong-position rendering.
instruction-visually-orphaned-from-its-f.scenario: Northwind Tickets checkout payment step. The Security code (#cvc) field's only cue about digit count and location is #cvc-note, which is absolutely positioned to the lower-left of the payment row and so renders beneath the full-width Card number field rather than beside the Security code input it actually governs; proximity attaches it to the wrong field.
instruction-visually-orphaned-from-its-f.note: Page demonstrates the aspect (rendered position attaches the instruction to the wrong field), but the prose described a different concrete instance: a Meridian Credit Union 'Link an external bank account' form where a CSS-grid routing-number hint lands beside the Account nickname field. The actual page is a Northwind Tickets checkout where a position:absolute CVC note lands under the Card number field.
